uncited: Regularization and Priors in NeRF training introduce constraints beyond photometric reconstruction to enforce physical plausibility, structural stability, and uncertainty awareness.
This family addresses issues such as scale ambiguity in material decomposition, instability in dynamically growing networks, and overfitting to noisy observations.

It is distinct from sibling methods like [Learning Rate Scheduling](2701-learning-rate-scheduling.md) or [Adam Optimisation with Adaptive Scaling](3093-adam-optimisation-with-adaptive-scaling.md) by modifying the loss landscape or network outputs directly rather than the optimization trajectory or parameter updates.

The core mechanism involves augmenting the primary photometric loss $\mathcal{L}_{photo}$ with auxiliary terms $\mathcal{L}_{reg}$ derived from domain-specific assumptions (e.g., smoothness, intrinsic decomposition, or probabilistic uncertainty).
where $\lambda_k$ are hyperparameters balancing the influence of each prior.
These priors often operate on intermediate representations (such as reflectance/shading fields or uncertainty maps) rather than just the final rendered pixel values.
Regularization in NeRFs evolved from basic $L_2$ losses to more sophisticated priors addressing specific failure modes.
Intrinsic decomposition priors (reflectance/shading) were developed to handle lighting variations and object insertion [4624-reflectance-and-shading-decomposition-priors.md].
Uncertainty-aware losses in multi-scale training address the instability of dynamically growing architectures [2967-multi-scale-joint-training-parameters.md].
